import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.8

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Part b), proposed by D. V. Anosov, asks whether there exists a non-cyclic finitely presented group
with an element such that every group element is conjugate to an integer power of that element.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.8»

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a quotient of a free group on finitely
many generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/--
Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ containing an element $a$ such that
every element of $G$ is conjugate to $a^n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.8».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬IsCyclic G ∧
      ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.8»

Interpreted “some power” as an integer power `a ^ n` with `n : ℤ`, as specified in the decomposition table.
Used Mathlib's `IsConj g (a ^ n)` for conjugacy and `¬IsCyclic G` for non-cyclicity.
Quantified the witness group in `Type`, following repository idiom for existentially quantified mathematical structures; every finitely presented group has such a small representative.

new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no predicate for a finitely presented group, and `Group.FG` expresses only finite generation.

namespace Kourovka.«8.8»

/--
A group is finitely presented if it is the quotient of a free group on finitely
many generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ f : FreeGroup (Fin n) →* G,
    Function.Surjective f ∧
      ∃ relators : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)),
        MonoidHom.ker f = Subgroup.normalClosure (relators : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))

/--
Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ containing an element
$a$ such that every element of $G$ is conjugate to $a^n$ for some
$n \in \mathbb{Z}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.8».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ IsCyclic G ∧
        ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.8»

Represented finite presentability by a surjective homomorphism from `FreeGroup (Fin n)` whose kernel is exactly the normal closure of a finite set of relators.
Used Mathlib's `IsConj g (a ^ n)`; in a group this says that a conjugate of `g` equals `a ^ n`, and conjugacy is symmetric.
Used `¬ IsCyclic G` for “non-cyclic” and kept finite presentability as a separate conjunct rather than weakening it to `Group.FG`.
Quantified `G : Type` following the repository's yes/no existential-group idiom.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.8

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Part b) of Problem 8.8, due to D. V. Anosov, asks whether there exists a non-cyclic
finitely presented group $G$ containing an element $a$ such that every element of
$G$ is conjugate to some power of $a$.

Mathlib has `Group.FG` for finitely generated groups but no notion of a finitely
presented group, so one is defined in this file: a group is finitely presented if it
is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite set `rels` of relators in the free
group on a finite set of generators.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.8»

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it has a presentation
$G \cong \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ with finitely many generators
and finitely many relations, i.e. $G$ is isomorphic to the quotient of the free group on a
finite type by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨α, _, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨_, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/-- The group `PresentedGroup rels` given by finitely many generators and finitely many
relators is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α] {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨α, inferInstance, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/--
(D. V. Anosov). Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ which contains an
element $a$ such that each element of $G$ is conjugate to some power of $a$?

Here "power" means an integer power $a^n$ with $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.8».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ IsCyclic G ∧
      ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.8»

modeling_decisions: 'Power of a' is read as an integer power `a ^ n` with `n : ℤ` (per the decomposition notes and standard group-theoretic usage); with `n : ℕ` the condition would be strictly stronger in general.

Finite presentability is defined via an isomorphism `G ≃* PresentedGroup rels` with `α : Type` finite and `rels` a finite set; this is the standard definition (equivalent to: some/any finite generating set plus a finitely normally generated relation subgroup of the free group). The generator type lives in `Type` while `G : Type*`; this is harmless since any finitely presented group is countable.

A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ with finitely many generators and
finitely many relators, i.e. to the quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the
normal closure of a finite set of relators.

  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_of_surjective (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _)
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/--
Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ which contains an element $a$
such that each element of $G$ is conjugate to some power of $a$?
